channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: JPMorganChase reports cyberattack on third-party service providers
item.description: JPMorganChase said on Thursday morning that third parties who provide services to the banking giant were the target of a cyberattack.

item.title: EU reveals it suffered 'AI-powered' cyber attack
item.description: The EU has revealed it suffered a cyber attack powered by AI last month and some of its digital tools are still offline as a result.

item.title: Gender pay gap: French women work "for free” from today
item.description: Women in Europe are still paid less than men, with the gap falling from 15.1% in 2016 to 11.1% in 2024, according to Eurostat. In France, women symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on Thursday, 19 November, and at the current pace equality would not be reached until 2062. Experts warn that AI could make things worse by eliminating administrative and legal jobs where many women work, while childbirth and short paternity leave continue to slow women’s careers.

item.title: 'GTA VI': A masterpiece? Fans react to gaming's biggest release
item.description: Critics are calling the new "Grand Theft Auto VI" a masterpiece. In this edition of arts24, we hear what fans make of one of the biggest video game releases in history. We also look at U2's new album and tour marking 50 years of the band, discover the French comic book that Pope Leo is reading and meet the women redefining Mexico's Mariachi tradition.

item.title: The chocolate countdown: The art of the advent calendar
item.description: The holiday season is almost upon us and with it come advent calendars. The annual physical countdown originated in 19th-century Germany as a Christian tradition to count down the days until Christmas. Eugénie Pont from the magazine Fou de Pâtisserie tells us more about what we can expect from the biggest chocolate makers in France.

item.title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
item.description: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

item.title: WATCH: Military family gets surprise of a lifetime at 2026 CMAs
item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.

item.title: Police 'examining' claims of women being trafficked by Epstein on King's Balmoral estate
item.description: Police are "examining" claims of women being trafficked by Jeffrey Epstein on the King's private Scottish estate, one of Britain's top cops has confirmed to Sky News.

item.title: Behind the UK's use of AI in asylum applications
item.description: The UK is increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage its immigration system, from analysing migrants’ phones to processing asylum applications. But what happens when AI gets involved in deciding how an asylum seeker's story is understood? Stella Elgersma, journalist at InfoMigrants, explains how the UK Home Office is testing AI tools to process asylum applications, including a system that generates summaries of asylum interviews. With errors, limited human oversight and concerns over transparency, could AI put asylum seekers’ lives at risk?

item.title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
item.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

item.title: Beaujolais Nouveau: A French tradition uncorked
item.description: Every year on the third Thursday of November, France raises a glass to one of its most joyful traditions: Le Beaujolais Nouveau! That means that this Thursday, millions of bottles of the 2026 young red wine will be uncorked around the world, from Lyon to New York. Olivier Badoureaux, wine expert and director of the French trade organisation Inter Beaujolais, tells us what we should expect from this year's vintage.

item.title: France: Retirees march against 2027 budget cuts
item.description: More than a thousand people marched in Paris on Thursday, called by a union alliance joined by student and high-school groups, to protest social and tax measures targeting retirees in the 2027 budgets. The government wants retirees to contribute about €5.4 billion, by freezing the indexation of pensions above €1,260 and reforming their 10% income tax allowance. Union leaders say the money should not come from retirees’ pockets, as FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago explains.

item.title: Anthropic begins trading as $1.5 trillion company in biggest IPO on record
item.description: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Thursday after pricing its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the artificial intelligence giant at $1.5 trillion and surpassing SpaceX as the largest initial public offering on record. The IPO puts to the test Wall Street's faith in ​the AI boom, pitting promises of the technology as an economic game-changer against fears of a market bubble and risks to humanity.

item.title: Chef Rachel Khoo: 'You don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious food'
item.description: One of the world's best-known chefs has spoken to FRANCE 24 about her new book that proves you certainly don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious meals. The book "The Smallest Restaurant in Paris" tells her own story of starting out in a tiny Parisian flat cooking food just for two people at a time. That then led to a BBC series and a decade of writing and filming cooking stories. Rachel Khoo is now a judge on "The Great Australian Bake Off". She spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: Trump-Putin-Xi meeting updates: Leaders at historic summit chart 'different course'
item.description: Trump participated on Thursday in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

item.title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
item.description: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
item.description: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.

item.title: 'Their lives, their rights, their history': Not the end of accountability for the Rohingya people'
item.description: Oliver Farry welcomes Sonya Sceats, Director and CEO of the British Institute of International and Comparative Law. The case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar before the ICJ, and the court ruling, both have great significance for the Rohingya people, the interpretation of the Genocide Convention and the possibility of future criminal proceedings. The case could also have important implications for South Africa's proceedings against Israel, where there are “many similarities between the two cases.”

item.title: What to know about Xi, Putin and Trump's historic trilateral summit
item.description: China's Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump met for a historic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, where they agreed on a "peace declaration". The three leaders pledged to reform the UN, increase supplies of refined petroleum products and uphold the immunity enjoyed by officials in international courts.

item.title: Poundland bosses warn of funding squeeze in fresh talks with minister
item.description: Poundland's bosses have told the government that the discount retailer faces a further funding crisis just days before a cliff-edge which could lead to its collapse.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's Voyager 1 now a light-day away after 1977 launch
item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: Putin vows to retaliate as Ukraine hits prized Crimea bridge for third time in four days
item.description: Ukraine has launched a third aerial attack in four days on the Kerch Bridge - a vital link between Russia and Crimea - with Vladimir Putin vowing retaliation.

item.title: WATCH: Man reunited with long-lost cat after 3.5 years
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.

item.title: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in the northern Rakhine State. (Image credit: Salahuddin Ahmed)

item.title: World Toilet Day is a funny idea with a serious goal: A world awash in toilets
item.description: Yahoo for the loo! November 19 marks the 25th anniversary of World Toilet Day. The theme this year: "Sanitation and Gender Equality: Safe Toilets, Equal Futures." (Image credit: John Poole/Ryan Kellman/NPR )

item.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI', a 'masterpiece' 13 years in the making
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 19: An historic trilateral summit takes place in Shenzhen between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. But is it more optics than substance? Also, a highly awaited decision from the International Court of Justice could redefine genocide. Finally, a huge cultural moment: "Grand Theft Auto VI" is out and the reviews are ecstatic.

item.title: Nigeria: States set to get their own police forces
item.description: Nigeria has moved a step closer to letting its 36 states set up their own police forces. The National Assembly has sent a constitutional amendment bill to the president, as authorities seek state-run police to complement the federal force amid growing insecurity. Many states currently fund vigilante groups to fight armed groups like Boko Haram, but these groups are poorly trained and ill-equipped for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent has the latest.

item.title: French 2027 presidential race: Green leader Tondelier draws closer to hard-left Mélenchon
item.description: Six months before the first round of France’s presidential election, Green party leader Marine Tondelier is moving closer to Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader of the radical left. The move has caught the other candidates on the left and in the centre off guard, notably Raphaël Glucksmann. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali explains.

item.title: Senegal: Pastef removes President Faye from its ranks
item.description: In Senegal, Pastef, the majority party led by National Assembly president Ousmane Sonko, has made official the departure of President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. It is the latest episode in a split with his former Prime minister that was already largely complete, and it comes in the middle of an economic crisis.

item.title: Myanmar's Rohingya case: how does the ICJ define genocide?
item.description: The ICJ is preparing to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a case brought by The Gambia after the 2017 crackdown. The key legal test is proving intent to destroy a group, which is notoriously hard, and the court’s reading of it could also weigh on South Africa’s case against Israel.

item.title: What to know before Anthropic goes public
item.description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic stands poised to go public at a valuation north of $1 trillion, marking a major test for the AI boom.

item.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of the House, incoming majority leader Katherine Clark discusses the party's ambitious agenda and divisions within its ranks. (Image credit: Anna Moneymaker)

item.title: AI lab Anthropic sets stock market record with $81 billion IPO
item.description: Anthropic becomes the first "pure play" AI lab to go public, with an eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation, a bellwether moment amid growing concerns of a financial bubble in the sector. Meanwhile, a scientific study shows US data centres are emitting as much greenhouse gas as entire nations.
